answer: Each identity binds to an island via a tide-resilient proof: solving atlas compression on curated datasets. Prior work is stored in a shared ledger. Fake identities must recompute unique paths, tied to their solve sequence. Every extra identity raises storage costs as prior paths become invalid, forcing 0.2s of non-parallelizable work per head to rebuild consistency. The cost is fixed per identity as each requires distinct recomputation and cannot share bulk storage.
